newsitem.title: USA: Texaco creating Louisiana NGL network.
newsitem.headline: Texaco creating Louisiana NGL network.

text.p: Texaco Inc said Tuesday TENDS -- Texaco Expanded NGL Distribution System -- will start full operations in early 1998.

The 500-mile pipeline network was designed by Texaco to distributre natural gas liquids safely and efficient to growing markets across South Louisiana, according to Robert G. Wells, executive vice president of Texaco Natural Gas Inc.

NGLs are liquid products derived from the production of natural gas and include ethane, propane, iso-butane, normal butane and natural gasoline. These products are used primarily as chemical feedstocks and specialty fuels at refineries.
TENDS, a network of pipelines capable of transporting a combined maximum of 230,000 barrels of product daily to refineries and petrochemical complexes, is expected to cost $70 million, Texaco said.
"Supplies of NGLs are rapidly increasing as more deepwater natural gas exploratory and development projects in the Gulf of Mexico commence production," Wells explained.

"Two of Texao's previously announced deepwater discoveries, Petronius and Gemini, are expected to commence initial oil and natural gas production by the end of 1999, expanding the supply of NGLs even further.

Primarily as a result of escalating offshore natural gas production, the company said, the volume of NGLs entering South Louisiana is expected to roughly dobule from about 290,000 barrels daily to 450,000-500,000 by the year 2000.
Production from the large deepwater projects usually contains greater amounts of NGLs than existing Gulf of Mexico production, Texaco explained.
The company said TENDS has already completed an $11.3 million acquisition of an 83 mile pipeline from Dow Chemical Co's Dow Intrastate Gas Co which was previously used to transport natural gas.

Texaco said an additional $3.5 million will be spent upgrading this 8-inch pipeline, which forms the western leg of TENDS, beginning at the company's fractionator located at the Henry Hub (near New Iberia) and extending to Sulphur, La.
It said this leg of the pipeline will provide NGL deliveries to Lake Charles, La., customers beginning this summer. ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
